question: Should OpenClaw add a target-agent-specific subagent concurrency contract, and should it live at `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` rather than introducing caller-selected named lanes?
rationale: The change adds public configuration and determines whether concurrency policy belongs to the target agent, spawning parent, or caller-selected lane; repository inspection cannot resolve that product contract safely.

options.title: Target-agent override
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce it beneath the existing global pool for every spawn targeting that agent.

options.title: Named spawn lanes
options.body: Use the broader caller-selected lane model tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10467, accepting additional tool and configuration complexity.

options.title: Keep global-only
options.body: Retain the shared cap and document separate gateways or external resource throttling as the operational workaround.

recommendation.title: Target-agent override
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce it beneath the existing global pool for every spawn targeting that agent.

likelyOwner.reason: They are most directly connected to the current resolver and lane configuration and already participated in reviewing this product gap.
